answer_1.quote: We conduct two experiments to assess if a large language model, GPT-3, can recognize dogwhistles.
answer_1.outputs: generated dogwhistles, identified covert meanings, toxicity scores

answer_2.quote: We calculate recall as the proportion of dogwhistles in our glossary that were also surfaced at least once by GPT-3. For precision, the authors manually inspect candidates...

answer_3.quote: We now consider a natural follow-up question: can LLMs correctly identify dogwhistles in real-world texts? ... We present a small manual analysis with ChatGPT/GPT-4 ... using several real-world examples from our glossary as a proof of concept for in-context dogwhistle recognition.

answer_4.quote: The first author manually evaluated whether or not each of the 5,760 GPT-3 generations contains the covert meaning for each dogwhistle.
answer_4.guideline: manually evaluated whether or not each generation contains the covert meaning for each dogwhistle
